headline: High: OpenBBTerminal can feed sensitive financial context into opik while opik’s broad egress raises leakage and cascading-error risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: OpenBBTerminal can use MCP and consumes files/APIs, while opik exposes a REST API and is not runnable, so a shared orchestration path is plausible but not directly documented. If OpenBBTerminal outputs are routed into opik without provenance checks, prompt-like content could be treated as instructions. The pairwise pathway is inferred, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF OpenBBTerminal outputs are forwarded into opik prompts or evaluation inputs without sanitization, injection risk exists.
IF a shared MCP or API bridge passes raw model text between the agents, opik may ingest attacker-controlled instructions.
mitigations: Add a provenance tag to every OpenBBTerminal output before forwarding.
Strip instruction-like prefixes from any text sent to opik.
Require a human review step for any cross-agent prompt content.
Disable the bridge unless the exact input schema is validated.

B_data_leakage.rationale: OpenBBTerminal touches financial, licensed, and public data, and opik has broad network egress. Even though opik has no declared data classes, sending OpenBBTerminal context to a remote backend could leak sensitive financial or licensed material. The interaction is not directly evidenced, but the pair creates a plausible default leakage path.
conditions: IF OpenBBTerminal context is transmitted to opik’s backend, financial or licensed data may leave the local boundary.
IF opik logs prompts or traces containing OpenBBTerminal outputs, those contents may persist remotely.
mitigations: Redact financial identifiers before handoff.
Send only minimal summaries to opik.
Turn off trace/log capture for cross-agent runs.
Use a local-only test dataset for integration checks.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: OpenBBTerminal cannot write the filesystem, modify git, or egress to the network, while opik only advertises broad network egress and a REST API. There is no documented overlapping write surface or shared mutable resource, so direct capability conflict is limited. Uncertainty remains because opik’s write surfaces are not fully described, but the known overlap is small.
conditions: IF opik is configured to write to a shared workspace or repository, conflicts could emerge.
IF an external orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same mutable resource, race conditions become possible.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Mount shared data read-only.
Avoid concurrent writes to any shared repo.
Document any orchestrator-level locking before enabling parallel runs.

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenBBTerminal can emit financial-modeling outputs through APIs/MCP, and opik is an evaluation/observability tool that may consume those outputs. If opik treats OpenBBTerminal results as authoritative, errors can cascade into misleading evaluations or downstream actions. The pairwise pathway is plausible but not directly documented, so medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF opik ingests OpenBBTerminal outputs without verification, incorrect financial facts can propagate.
IF downstream automation uses opik’s evaluated results as ground truth, a single upstream error can cascade.
mitigations: Require source citations on all OpenBBTerminal-derived claims.
Add a verification step before opik scores or forwards results.
Flag low-confidence outputs for manual review.
Limit downstream actions to read-only reporting until validated.

E_compliance.rationale: OpenBBTerminal explicitly touches financial and licensed data, while opik’s profile lacks residency, retention, and certification details. That mismatch creates a compliance gap if the pair processes regulated financial or licensed material through opik’s remote observability path. Because opik’s compliance posture is undocumented, uncertainty escalates to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF regulated financial or licensed data is sent from OpenBBTerminal into opik, retention and residency obligations may be implicated.
IF opik stores traces outside the required jurisdiction, compliance controls may be violated.
mitigations: Exclude regulated datasets from cross-agent runs.
Confirm retention settings before enabling traces.
Use synthetic or anonymized inputs for evaluation.
Record the data-flow boundary in an operator checklist.
